name: C2C Advanced Systems Limited
summary: Completed forensic review and conditional five-year rescue models support an evidence hold, not an investable defence-growth thesis. Five-year cash burn, collection delays and unresolved reporting/review questions prevent dependable growth and return scores despite new orders.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: C2C has disclosed substantial defence-integration orders, but financing and cash realization dominate the investment case. FY26 sales grew 26.5% while PAT fell 36.4%; five years of reported operating cash flow total −₹177.43 crore. Current primary filings do not resolve the NSE-appointed historical review or establish dependable collection/funding. Completed annual rescue models are conditional illustrations, not an expected base case: reference terminal ₹191.75/3.07% CAGR versus 19 October ₹164.85, bear zero residual equity and bull ₹662.22/32.06%. No probability-weighting or numeric IAS is warranted. An unresolved evidence hold is not a finding of fraud. [S1][S3][S4][S5][S7][S13][S90]

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: C2C Advanced Systems Limited, ISIN INE0U7V01015, NSE C2C/SM, SME as of 20 October 2026. Active SM capital 16,968,433 shares matches FY26 statements; stale SQ capital is not used. Official 19 October close ₹164.85 and 150-share lot are dated observations, not live execution. Standalone Ind AS accounts include USA branch audited by a CPA; branch is not a consolidated subsidiary. Audited March 2026 opening balances anchor five synthetic forecast years, not a claim about October cash. FY27 half-year results were not identified in the reviewed cutoff cache. Model hurdles 15%, reference liquidity ₹5 lakh. G1/G2/G3 hold unresolved; G4 conditional. Historical disclosure confidence high, economic recoverability/normalization low; overall low. [S1][S3][S90][S91]

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: Supported factors distinguish weak quality from missing evidence: GOV 3, MOAT 3, DUR 3, CAP 2, CASH 1, BAL 2, EXEC 2; REV and EARN remain NS because disputed historical transaction support and unquantified adjustments obstruct reliable quality inputs, not because arithmetic was omitted. Reported growth is calculated separately. CAP 2 uses low reported return on substantial equity/debt/lease capital including CWIP; no write-down is excluded merely to flatter returns. GOV 3 caps applicable BQS/IAS at 3; persistent CASH 1/CAP 2 caps applicable GQS 5. Missing-factor bounds retain original weights; no renormalized score or midpoint. D1/P2/L8 are supported, R remains NS because funding/recovery cannot be assigned a defensible expected reference. G2 excludes ranking independently of score arithmetic. [S1][S3][S4][S5][S6][S7][S90][S96]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: C2C integrates mission computing, command/control/data fusion, hardware/software and industrial systems. FY26 domestic sales ₹2.4671 crore versus exports ₹143.1752 crore; service purchases ₹59.7828 crore and equipment/software ₹17.9969 crore prevent treating all revenue as proprietary SaaS. Contract milestones, acceptance, field integration and supplier dependence matter. June order covers 30 counter-drone subunits and integration with previously contracted computing systems. Kilo’s maritime-simulator alliance and IIT Ropar/Aaizel research framework extend capabilities but are not guaranteed sales. A single segment does not imply uniform cash economics. [S1][S13][S15][S16]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Systems integration knowledge, military-domain personnel and repeat programme scope can create switching costs once accepted. The June follow-on order is positive evidence. Against that, prospectus customer concentration was top 5 = 89.59% FY24/99.05% H1 FY25; long acceptance/collection cycles and third-party components constrain pricing power. Defence demand does not prove proprietary IP monetization. Data Patterns’ rugged electronics/test equipment and Paras’ optics/EMP/heavy-engineering businesses are structural comparators, not interchangeable multiple benchmarks. Their manufacturing/IP mix differs; no current peer valuation premium is imported without comparable cash quality. MOAT 3 reflects an unproven commercial advantage, not an assertion that no technical capability exists. [S1][S4][S13][S20][S21]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Reported revenue ₹0.3469/8.0487/41.0589/115.1111/145.6423 crore FY22–26. FY23–26 CAGR 162.5% and latest 26.5% describe reported scale, not verified sustainable quality; the near-zero FY22 base is unsuitable for promotion to a high REV score. Prospectus FY24 PAT ₹12.3954 crore is before ₹0.1185 crore prior-period tax versus later annual ₹12.2769; FY25 ₹28.8395 and FY26 ₹18.3296. June disclosed order exceeds ₹80 crore, 30% advance and 70% completion payment within three months, calendar 2026 execution. Receipt of contractual advance is not demonstrated merely by order announcement. April order amount is undisclosed. No double counting of pipeline/MoUs as orderbook or revenue. [S1][S3][S4][S13][S14]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: FY26 net receivables ₹240.2955 crore, inventory ₹62.0568, CWIP ₹26.6674 and other current assets ₹29.4095 require cash before accounting growth benefits owners. Broad EBIT excluding other income is PBT 27.4356 + finance 8.7035 − other 16.0317 = ₹20.1074. A stricter operating proxy adds back only loan and lease interest 7.0678, retaining tax/DBO/other interest as economic costs: EBIT ₹18.4717 and 25% tax proxy NOPAT ₹13.8538. Closing capital equity 236.4777 + debt 45.3155 + lease 9.1506 − cash .9316 = ₹290.0122, giving 4.78% closing-capital return, not average ROIC. Including CWIP is intentional. ECL suppression is not a free normalization: pre-ECL profit is collectible only if assets realize. New orders and advance terms improve potential runway, but unverified receipts, supplier/tax obligations and promoter-funding dependence constrain reinvestment. [S1][S7][S13]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: The January 2025 BDO limited review covered April 2021–September 2024, questioned support for selected transactions and disclosure consistency; it was neither a statutory audit nor a judicial finding. The issuer disputes its findings; FY26 Note 36 says its response remains under NSE consideration. ICRA’s September 2025 report also recorded vendor-verification/bank-trail limits and allocation concerns, alongside the issuer’s explanation that vendors operate multiple business lines and supplied IT requirements. No current clearance or misappropriation finding is inferred. FY26 audit qualifies statutory-compliance matters and identifies related control weakness; management says CSR was subsequently paid and labour advice obtained, without a quantified reconciliation here. July 18 filing reports ₹2.95 lakh paid 12 July for delayed results, attributes delay to USA branch data and says compliance restored. This fine is separate from BDO. LABS resignation cites preoccupation after completing audit, not management interference; replacement appointed September 7. September CEO admits collection/update slippage; August reported ₹15.56 crore collected through July is positive but not cure. October director changes do not raise capital.  [S1][S2][S5][S6][S7][S8][S12][S17][S18]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text: Reported CFO FY22–26 −₹4.1581/−4.8100/−35.2720/−115.2350/−17.9512 crore; persistent cash weakness survives ordinary reclassification. FY26 receivables absorbed ₹144.791 crore, partly financed by payables ₹59.0843 and other financial asset release ₹23.6179. Net receivables follow gross ₹254.8339 less ECL ₹14.5384; 76% Indian receivable confirmations at audit are not collections, while USA relies on branch audit. Gross ageing includes ₹74.933 crore over one year. FY26 FX gain ₹15.2705 exceeds half PBT and is excluded from recurring model EBIT. FY25 P&L finance .9179 versus CF addback/deduction .4505, and FY26 operating lease movement .4443, require classification reconciliation; no invented clean adjusted CFO. Note 15 payables ₹61.8151 versus ageing ₹2.3589 differs ₹59.4562, visually confirmed, with no explicit branch reconciliation located; full BS liability used. Book OD .5090 is unpresented cheques, not bank facility. Current tax provision 11.1427/statutory dues 1.3043 are cash uses, not ignored. FY26 share allotment 327265@581 and issue expense .9765 reconcile gross 19.0141 to 18.0376 net CF; 179306 warrants 25% paid 2.6044 already in opening cash/equity, no repeat addition. [S1][S3][S4]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: Dated market cap ₹279.72 crore; reported FY26 EPS ₹10.8022 implies 15.26× PE, but FX/noncollection make this neither cheapness proof nor normalized earnings. Annual linked models separately bridge recoverable legacy receivables, inventory/other asset impairment, new WC, settlement of old creditors/taxes, capex, lease principal, debt and dilution. Reference ₹140/154/169.4/186.34/204.974 crore sales, 16% EBIT margin, 60% net legacy receivable recovery over five years, 45% new receivable/30% inventory/7% other asset/12% payable ratios, ₹2/2/2.5/3/3 capex and 9× terminal EBIT are assumptions. Noncash impairment ₹117.3524 reduces opening recoverable WC; deducted PAT and added back CFO, not second cash loss. Borrowing 10% matches reported promoter agreement; new draws charge half-year, 14% stress included. ₹60 crore ceiling is authorization not commitment; lease-inclusive ceiling/no incremental debt/equity at 50% quote sensitivities expose funding dependence. Reference first year requires ₹14.4885 new debt; terminal ₹191.75/3.07% CAGR not an expected forecast. Bear terminal 0/bull ₹662.22; bull assumes 90% legacy recovery, 22% margin and 13× exit. No fresh IPO cash or July receipts double-counted. Annual balance does not prove intrayear solvency or advance receipt. No dividends. [S1][S6][S7][S8][S10][S11][S90]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: Bear 20% net legacy receivable recovery, inventory 50%/other assets 40%, 8% margin, stagnant sales and 5× exit requires ₹89.35 crore hypothetical equity at 75% of dated quote even with funded debt allowed up to 60; terminal enterprise value does not cover net debt/leases, leaving zero equity. If such funding fails, continued operations cannot be assumed: the model is not an assurance of survival. Court/statutory penalties are unquantified; ₹5 crore bear cash charge is an analyst stress, not estimated fine. Supplier payment compression, FX reversal, acceptance failures or promoter withdrawal can worsen it. June advance payment terms and actual July receipts are contrary evidence, not ignored. [S1][S7][S8][S10][S13]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: At unchanged 1.6968433 crore shares, 5×/10× dated price require approximately ₹1398.6/2797.2 crore equity. At 9× EBIT and 16% margin, ignoring additional net debt/dilution and holding terminal cash around ₹25.94, implied revenue is about ₹953/1924 crore, roughly 46%/68% five-year growth from FY26. These are generous reverse-value thresholds, not linked forecasts: working capital at 60% net intensity would consume hundreds of additional crores and could dilute owners. Completed bull ends ₹662.22, only 4.02× current price, even with 90% legacy recovery, 22% margin and 13× exit. Thus neither 5× nor 10× is demonstrated by completed scenarios or announced orders. [S1][S13][S90]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: First require cash bank evidence matched to legacy invoice/customer ageing, not a percentage of unspecified expected collections; distinguish June order advance from legacy cash. Obtain NSE review disposition and issuer response, current IPO monitoring, payable ageing scope and USA branch details, quantified statutory liabilities and lease CF bridge. Monitor replacement auditor opinions, SOFTEX/export regularization and actual funding/allotment terms. G3 cannot clear on borrowing authorization alone. At 19 October all 60 sessions observed; 60 day median ₹2.1210 crore/day supports ₹5 lakh exit in 0.47 days at 5% participation, 1.18 days at 2%, subject to depth/circuit locks. 150 lot ₹24727.50; 20 lots ₹494550. REG1 flags large historical high/low variation and SME trading caution, effective 21 October; named ASM/GSM/ESM no match is not universal clearance. Do not invent missing days from generic caution. [S1][S7][S10][S11][S90][S91][S92][S93][S94][S96]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Evidence hold/high-risk special situation, not compounder or clean value candidate. Substantial review and completed conditional models do not make economic recovery or funding knowable. Numeric BQS/GQS/IAS remain NS with supported factor coverage and bounds preserved; no ranked recommendation or allocation. Re-open only after collection/liability/review/funding evidence materially improves. At that point rebuild opening cash/share count rather than reuse March balances or assume proposed warrants issued. [S1][S5][S6][S7][S10][S11]

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Primary annual/prospectus/history, public limited review, monitoring reports and April–October events were actually reviewed; failed old issuer prospectus URL was replaced by merchant banker copy. Selected peer product pages support business comparison only, not current peer PE. Financial liability/recoverability questions remain after reasonable primary-source searches, not because a numeric model was unperformed. Scenarios are conditional assumptions with reproducible cash/debt/equity bridges; new financing not guaranteed, no response probabilities invented. The July utilization certificate is not mistaken for a full BDO rebuttal. [S1][S3][S4][S5][S6][S19][S20][S21]

GOV.reason: Current qualified audit/control weakness and unresolved historical review/monitoring questions outweigh issuer rebuttals and reported fine payment; no fraud assertion.

MOAT.reason: Integration capability and follow-on order positive; concentration/vendor reliance and unverified pricing power limit advantage.

REV.reason: Reported growth arithmetic known; limited review transaction questions and unresolved receivable validation make quality confidence Low, so NS rather than a forced high score.

DUR.reason: New orders/alliances offer pathway, but legacy cash/funding constraints severely limit self-funded runway.

CAP.reason: Reported core NOPAT yield only 4.78% on closing full capital including CWIP; unproductive legacy capital cannot be excluded to flatter return. Contract advances are positive prospective counterevidence.

CASH.reason: Five consecutive cash negative years and latest collections below expectations; actual reported July receipts positive but insufficient to cure.

BAL.reason: Large book equity and promoter 10% loans support operations, but tiny cash, debt/lease/current tax and creditor obligations plus unverified asset recovery dominate.

EXEC.reason: New order delivery opportunity and partial cash receipts offset by documented collection/update failures, delayed results and control weakness.

EARN.reason: FX gain, ECL recoverability, unquantified statutory effects and cash flow classification obstruct normalized earnings quality; NS despite reported PAT decline being known.

R.reason: Completed conditional models but no evidence-grounded expected reference for the recovery/funding assumptions; NS not missing calculation.

D.reason: Bear enterprise value does not cover net financial liabilities even after hypothetical equity; funding shortfall can stop operations.

P.reason: Headline 15.26 PE hides FX/collection risk; conditional reference only 3.07% return before unquantified liabilities, so little margin of safety.

L.reason: Complete 60 observed history/150 lot and <.5 day 5% exit positive; high-low volatility cautions and circuit/depth risk prevent top score.

ranking_eligibility.reason: Incomplete factors and critical evidence hold; bounds are mathematical missing-data bounds, not valuations or ranking scores.
